By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 06:43 EST, 18 November 2026.

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his upcoming agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

Industry observers note that it’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel.

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move.

He is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

Industry observers note that gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a recent development, in a farewell post on Instagram he mentioned: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with major dreams.

'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

Sources indicate that 'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

In a recent development, 'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'.

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of looks in first team training sessions this season.

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

According to recent reports, A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

Sources indicate that southampton had a mixed summer transfer window but one major blow was the sale of Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The Saints brought in multiple defenders in a bid to replace him and one of which was Zach Abbott who joined on loan.

Abbott has since struggled for gametime and fellow summer signing Keven Schlotterbeck has impressed but is now out injured. With that in mind, Tonda Eckert may may be hoping to bring in another centre-back during the January window.

Industry observers note that southampton are in an excellent position to push for automatic promotion this season, something that they cannot afford to take any risks with. With that in mind, they should be keeping an eye on Torbjorn Heggem’s situation.

The former West Brom man looks likely to leave Bologna this January, sparking talk of a return to the Baggies. However, while talk of a move to the Hawthorns has been quashed, a move to Southampton should be under consideration.

The 27-year-old has struggled for regular opportunities under Raffaele Palladino and has made it clear that he does not want to spend the remainder of the season sitting on the bench.

With the January transfer window approaching, the Saints could have an opportunity to bring an established international back to English football.

Heggem joined Bologna from West Brom in August 2025 after an impressive Championship campaign. He has since made 45 appearances for the Serie A side, but his involvement has decreased this season. That could leave Southampton well placed to explore a deal.

In a recent development, the Norwegian international has already demonstrated his ability to perform in the Championship. During the 2024/25 campaign, he made 45 league appearances for West Brom, scoring once and providing two assists. His consistency earned him both the Players’ Player of the Season and Supporters’ Player of the Season awards, underlining how highly regarded he was at The Hawthorns.

Heggem offers physical presence, aerial ability and impressive distribution. He is naturally a centre-back but can also operate at left-back, while his preference for his left foot makes him an especially useful defensive option.

His current Serie A statistics also demonstrate his technical qualities. Across seven appearances and 525 minutes this season, he has completed 93.4 per cent of his passes, recorded 43 line-breaking passes and made 27 clearances. He has also won 12 aerial duels and earned 25 caps for Norway.

Southampton would face competition for his signature, and his wages could prove a stumbling block. Nevertheless, he is approaching his prime, has proven himself in the Championship and possesses experience at a higher level.

With promotion ambitions potentially shaping their January business, Southampton should seriously consider swooping for Heggem. He could be an outstanding addition to their defensive options.

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

According to recent reports, so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

In a recent development, “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba remarked. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Recent findings suggest that floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

Sources indicate that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

In a recent development, allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Recent findings suggest that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has mentioned supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca mentioned.

According to recent reports, cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

Sources indicate that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

According to recent reports, nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

It has been revealed that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

Sources indicate that A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

It has been revealed that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

It has been revealed that significant cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

In a recent development, his shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Recent findings suggest that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Sources indicate that norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Sources indicate that norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

According to recent reports, and Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Industry observers note that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

Industry observers note that and without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

In a recent development, as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

In a recent development, samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

It has been revealed that A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Recent findings suggest that samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

It has been revealed that he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Sources indicate that norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic highlights some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Sources indicate that norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

Recent findings suggest that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Industry observers note that speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY.

Manchester City or Norwich vs Brighton.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EST, 18 November 2026.

Aston Villa have been told their Champions League clash with Galatasaray on Tuesday will still take place at the home of the Turkish champions despite the worrying state of the pitch.

Galatasaray have switched their home league fixture against Samsunspor this weekend to the stadium of top-flight rivals Istanbul Basaksehir to save the playing surface from further punishment.

Images released this week show a pitch that appears to be in alarming condition, with Galatasaray working around the clock to ensure it is playable. The club are in dialogue with UEFA.

At this stage, Daily Mail Sport understands UEFA are satisfied that the pitch will be in suitable condition when the sides take the field, though a pitch inspection will take place at 10am local time as is the case before any European fixture.

UEFA Article 5 states: ‘The field of play must be smooth and level and comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game.’.

Villa will look to strengthen their position in the league phase after winning three of their opening four games, though they lost their last fixture, at Barcelona.

Galatasaray are working around the clock to ensure their pitch is up to standard for their Champions League clash against Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Unai Emery’s men have already beaten Turkish opposition this term, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 for their record European win, though that fixture was at Villa Park.

After the chaotic 4-4 draw at Manchester United before the international break, Villa meet Sunderland at home in the Premier League on Saturday.

Emery has doubts over Matty Cash and Johan Manzambi, who picked up injuries while on international duty and may struggle to recover in time.

£1.2m Blackburn Rovers man has a chance to lock down a starting spot, beginning with crucial Burnley tie: Opinion

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday.
  • Recent findings suggest that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu.
  • Summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday. It’s a substantial occasion at Ewood Park, not only because of the rivalry, but because it marks Rovers’ first game since Tony Mowbray stepped back as head coach due to health complications earlier this week.

Recent findings suggest that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu. The Nigerian international has undergone surgery on his knee and is set to be sidelined until the Fresh Year.

Summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City. And, he played the full 90 minutes against West Ham while the medical staff waited for a verdict on Alebiosu’s blow.

Now that we know how long Blackburn Rovers’ go-to right-back will be out for, Beyuku has a real chance to make the starting role his own.

Most clubs have at least two players to cover in every position, and that is the case at Blackburn Rovers. With Alebiosu out, Beyuku is the only natural senior right-back available for selection, paving the way for him to come into the side.

According to recent reports, A reported fee of around £1.2m was paid to sign the 20-year-old from Modena in the summer, so there is clear belief in his potential. It was widely expected that Beyuku would be cover and competition for Alebiosu, but the injury thrusts him into the limelight.

He’s shown signs of growing into Championship football early on as well. His second-half against West Ham was the best we’ve seen from Beyuku to date, offering a lively presence up and down the right-hand side.

The Frenchman saw to his duties at the back with 10 defensive contributions, but he was forward-thinking and frequently involved in possession like Alebiosu as well. Beyuku completed 26 of his 29 passes, nine of which were line-breaking.

He was dispossessed twice, but this does come with the territory of being a progressive right-back who is still developing and settling into a newly introduced league (all stats via FotMob).

Recent findings suggest that alebiosu’s shoes are substantial ones to fill. It might not have been planned that Beyuku would assume a starting role this early into his Blackburn Rovers, given his age and need to grow into Championship football.

It means that, despite the fact he needs to deliver, there should be an element of patience.

If Johnson and Dodds feel Beyuku needs to be taken out of the side, there are options to consider. Kristi Montgomery has a key role in midfield alongside Sam Morsy but he has covered at right-back before. Matty Litherland is working his way back from injury too, while Lewis Miller is a longer-term absentee.

Industry observers note that beyuku will have the firm backing of the Rovers faithful. A strong display against arch-rivals Burnley this Sunday would be a sure-fire way for the youngster to endear himself to the fans and announce himself in Championship football.

  • Leicester City are eyeing an immediate promotion back from League One to the Championship this season under the guidance of head coach Russell Martin.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Foxes should target a move for Hull City attacking midfielder Kieran Dowell this winter to boost their chances of going up.
  • Dowell, 29, has played only once for the East Yorkshire outfit in the Carabao Cup so far in this campaign and a change of scene will do him good.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City are eyeing an immediate promotion back from League One to the Championship this season under the guidance of head coach Russell Martin. LCFC slipped out of the second tier earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with Sheffield Wednesday and Oxford United.

Recent findings suggest that the Foxes should target a move for Hull City attacking midfielder Kieran Dowell this winter to boost their chances of going up. The Merseyside-born man is expected to leave the Tigers after being left out of their 25-man squad in the Premier League.

Dowell, 29, has played only once for the East Yorkshire outfit in the Carabao Cup so far in this campaign and a change of scene will do him good. He is out of contract at the MKM Stadium in June next year after they handed him an 18-month deal last January when he signed.

Recent findings suggest that dowell would give Leicester City more competition and depth in their attacking department. He could also inject more quality into LCFC’s squad.

He played with Foxes’ midfielder John Lundstram at Hull City last term. The pair helped the Tigers win the play-offs and reach the top flight against the odds.

Industry observers note that dowell’s game time has dried up under Sergej Jakirovic since then though and he is now surplus to requirements. He was offered to Sheffield United in the summer but nothing materialised on that front in the end and he stayed put beyond the last deadline.

The ex-England youth international is available now though and landing him would be a statement of intent by Leicester City if they managed to get him. He will surely have interest from the division above but the prospect of regular minutes could turn his head.

Dowell had a spell in League One with Birmingham City in 2025. He helped the Blues win the title under Chris Davies.

According to recent reports, therefore, he knows what it takes to get out of Leicester City’s league. His experience would come in very handy for LCFC and he would be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room.

In a recent development, dowell rose up through Everton’s academy as a youngster. He has also had stints at Sheffield United, Derby County, Norwich City, Wigan Athletic, Norwich City and Rangers.

A deal wouldn’t break the bank, and it could give Russell Martin a valuable extra creative spark.

Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

📅 18 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.
  • Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.
  • It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

It has been revealed that one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

It has been revealed that “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel remarked. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

In a recent development, “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

In a recent development, even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He remarked: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

Recent findings suggest that “If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

In a recent development, “I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

Industry observers note that “It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I stated, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he remarked: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

According to recent reports, on Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

Tuchel stated that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

In a recent development, it was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”.

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

It has been revealed that “It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

In a recent development, “The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a newly introduced level of pressure.”.

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

It has been revealed that again, not something anyone has mentioned to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”.

In a recent development, tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Industry observers note that sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to indicates he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”.

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

Industry observers note that “When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”.

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel notes the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”.

Sources indicate that tuchel states his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He states the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has remarked the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Industry observers note that tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

Recent findings suggest that no questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

In a recent development, ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”.

Sources indicate that “They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”.

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

Jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

According to recent reports, the major ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Hopefully Thomas Tuchel will explain all later.

The absence of Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White is puzzling.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the top-scoring Englishman in the Premier League since the start of last season.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN STICKS IT IN!" pic.twitter.com/UJ54wPGytV.

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a upcoming Uefa Nations League campaign.

The head coach has selected a 27-man squad for the four-game window, which takes place between September 21 and October 6.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the fresh campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

And there’s a place in the squad for Trent Alexander-Arnold, alongside his Real Madrid teammate Jude Bellingham.

Sources indicate that here it is! 🤩Thomas Tuchel's first #ThreeLions squad of the 2026-27 season 🦁 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿.

Ivan Toney likely to miss out as he is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

Nine weeks have passed since the agonising semi-final collapse to Argentina and Tuchel can expect a grilling about his reflections.

He will need to rebuild trust with supporters heading into a cycle that culminates with a home Euros in 2028.

Eberechi Eze could be left out of the England squad announced this morning by Thomas Tuchel ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. The Arsenal midfielder has made six appearances for his club so far this season but has only started two of those games and none in the Premier League.

The 28-year-old played four times for England during the last World Cup but Tuchel is expected to shake up his forward options. There is an expectation that there will be a recall for Chelsea’s Cole Palmer.

The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.
  • The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

Industry observers note that 'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

According to recent reports, joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Sources indicate that post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Industry observers note that eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

3 left-backs West Ham must eye as after Scott Parker makes January transfer demands

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham must first navigate a busy December schedule before the January transfer window opens, but Scott Parker is already planning to strengthen his squad.
  • Recent findings suggest that the left-back role has been an matter for WHU this season after the departure of El Hadji Malick Diouf.
  • Industry observers note that adama Boiro was brought in late in the summer window but he has managed just 13 minutes of league action since his arrival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham must first navigate a busy December schedule before the January transfer window opens, but Scott Parker is already planning to strengthen his squad. The Hammers boss has identified two key positions he wants to address, with a newly introduced striker and left-back both on his January wish list.

Recent findings suggest that the left-back role has been an matter for WHU this season after the departure of El Hadji Malick Diouf. Academy duo Ezra Mayers and Ollie Scarles have had opportunities in that role but have failed to nail down the spot.

Industry observers note that adama Boiro was brought in late in the summer window but he has managed just 13 minutes of league action since his arrival. There only other option in that role has been Morato but he is a natural centre-back.

With that noted, here are three left-backs that could solve Scott Parker’s complications at West Ham….

Harrison Burrows brings a different, more attacking dimension from left-back. At Sheffield United he has posted strong goal and assist numbers while operating as a left-back or wing-back, showing he can contribute in the final third as well as defend.

That end product is useful for a West Ham side that needs more threat from deeper areas. Energetic in the press and capable of overlapping or underlapping, he adds balance to a back line that has often lacked a specialist left-sided option.

Sources indicate that while he has no prior Parker connection, his Championship pedigree and creative output make him a sensible complementary target alongside more defensively oriented options. He would give Parker a player who can both protect and progress.

Recent findings suggest that lucas Pires stands out because of his direct experience under Parker. During Burnley’s 2024/25 Championship promotion campaign he was a regular starter at left-back, logging a high number of appearances in a side that prioritised defensive organisation and controlled possession.

That familiarity with Parker’s demands is valuable for West Ham, who are still bedding in a newly introduced system. At Championship level he has shown reliability in one-v-one defending, solid positioning and the ability to recycle possession calmly.

Still only in his mid-twenties and presently at Burnley, he represents a realistic, modest-fee option rather than a high-risk gamble. His prior success in Parker’s set-up reduces the adaptation period and gives West Ham a proven, system-ready left-back who has already contributed to a promotion.

According to recent reports, harry Amass offers a high-upside profile that fits a promotion-chasing side. At 19 he has already accumulated meaningful Championship minutes on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City, demonstrating he can handle the physical and technical demands of the division.

Athletic, left-footed and comfortable stepping into midfield, he provides both defensive cover and progressive carrying from the back. Limited first-team opportunities at Manchester United make a permanent or long-term move plausible, and he has been repeatedly linked with West Ham.

It has been revealed that for Parker, Amass represents a younger, more dynamic alternative who can grow into the role over multiple seasons while still delivering immediate Championship quality. His age, athletic traits and proven second-tier experience make him an attractive, future-proof target.

#107065. Newcastle Confidential: Major revision on fresh £1.3bn super stadium as secret meeting with Wall Street money men is revealed, Amar Dedic bow and arrow case resolved and Joelinton injury boost

Newcastle Confidential: Major revision on fresh £1.3bn super stadium as secret meeting with Wall Street money men is revealed, Amar Dedic bow and arrow case resolved and Joelinton injury boost

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a newly introduced £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.
  • I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular newly introduced 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a newly introduced £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular newly introduced 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium aims is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a upcoming stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is right now the preference.

In a recent development, there has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a latest, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it.

In a recent development, in April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the new, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated.

Plans of the latest stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

Sources indicate that the proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious intends into a financially viable reality.

Industry observers note that sources have described the circular design of a new stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

Industry observers note that club sources say they are continuing to work on options and prepares for a newly introduced stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a newly introduced stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out.

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

However, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’.

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

Sources indicate that I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

It has been revealed that I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures.

Newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

Sources indicate that marong and Saine played in a 6-0 win over the i2i International Soccer Academy on Friday, and winger Saine chipped in with two assists. However, while there is a feeling both will secure moves to Europe in due course, Newcastle will keep a watching brief for now.

It has been revealed that the pair are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and were identified by the club’s new global talent team. They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

Neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

Both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

When the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

Sources indicate that in another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

According to recent reports, joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

It has been revealed that arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

The club tried to sign Trafford on three occasions under Eddie Howe, and even as recently as this summer he appeared destined for Tyneside.

So, with thanks to the idea from Ian Spencer, here is the ‘what might have been’ XI of Newcastle targets who came close to signing….

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

Would this XI beat the current side? Answers in the comments below please!

220-appearance star still without a club after summer departure from Leicester City

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City’s rapid decline from the Premier League to League One means there has been a lot of change over the past two years.
  • Industry observers note that among the mainstays in the Foxes’ Premier League days was right-back Ricardo Pereira, who joined from FC Porto in 2018 and grew into a starring role at the King Power Stadium.
  • Pereira stayed throughout Leicester City’s yo-yo years, but when his contract came to an end earlier this year, it was decided that he would move on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City’s rapid decline from the Premier League to League One means there has been a lot of change over the past two years. LCFC’s place as European football contenders is a thing of the past, and so are many of the players.

Industry observers note that among the mainstays in the Foxes’ Premier League days was right-back Ricardo Pereira, who joined from FC Porto in 2018 and grew into a starring role at the King Power Stadium. He was one of the league’s best in his position, but injuries hit and limited his involvement.

Pereira stayed throughout Leicester City’s yo-yo years, but when his contract came to an end earlier this year, it was decided that he would move on. And, over four months on from his release, he remains out of the game.

Pereira managed 39 appearances in Leicester City’s relegation season, proving he can still manage a demanding season despite previous injury problems.

Sources indicate that his pedigree at the very top of the game with the Foxes and Porto has seen him grow into a leadership figure over the years. The experience he has to his name is of huge value to younger players and his character would rapidly see him become an influential figure in the dressing room.

Recent findings suggest that granted, the speed and physical traits Pereira showed at his best aren’t as strong anymore. However, he has always been a technically gifted player in possession, and his pedigree helps him read the game well.

Pereira has shared images and videos of himself training during his time without a team. He would need time to get up to speed to play full games at a competitive level, but he has kept himself ticking over as he awaits his next opportunity after leaving LCFC.

It remains to be seen just what awaits Pereira after a long spell out of the game. Opportunities do dry up as the season moves on from the summer transfer window, so there might not be many intriguing options out there.

In a recent development, the MLS regular season has just ended, so the Leicester City man could join a team for their 2027 preparations to be ready to go for the new campaign. Alternatively though, Pereira may wish to see out the latter years of his career back in his home country of Portugal.

Teams in Liga Portugal would certainly benefit from his leadership and experience. Having broken through in his home country before leaving for bigger things, it could be a fitting end to his career to return and become an influential player for a top flight side.

Tech Report: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
